newsitem.title: sri lanka: UN report says S.Lanka defence bill rising faster.
newsitem.headline: UN report says S.Lanka defence bill rising faster.

text.p: Nations report said on Thursday that Sri Lanka's defence expenditure was rising faster than most developing countries and that it had one of the highest rateS of official development assistance (ODA) in Asia.

The United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) 1997 annual human development report said Sri Lanka's defence bill rose to 4.9 percent of the gross domestic product (GDP) between 1985 and 1995 while the average for the rest of the developing world fell to 3.1 percent from 7.1 percent over the same period.
The report said Sri Lanka also had a high rate of ODA when compared to rest of Asia. At $31 per capita, it receives nearly three times the average of $11 for developing countries.
The report said India received only $2 per capita of ODA, Pakistan $6, Bangladesh $11 and China $3.
But it praised Sri Lanka for its efforts towards gender equality, saying women fared relatively well in this Indian Ocean island.

The report said women in Sri Lanka will live eight years longer than most of their counterparts in other developing nations, and that 17 percent of managers and administrators were women compared to a 10 percent average in the developing world.

But in ranking Sri Lanka 91st out of 175 countries on a human development index the report said 57 percent of Sri Lankans did not have access to safe water and about eight percent were not expected to survive to age 40.
It said 94 percent of the people in the island had access to health services and infant mortality was a low 19 per 1,000 against an average of 58 for the world.
